label: prop:deuteron-binding-dressing-proton-net
title: The deuteron binding dressing $(1-\tfrac{h}{2})$ is the proton NF net coefficient
html:
Conditional on Quarks as Borromean-linked unknots in the exceptional divisor. Let h = q - q^{-1} and \mathfrak{E}_0 = m_e/(q(q-1)). Let \mathrm{net}(p) = 1 - \tfrac{h}{2} and \mathrm{net}(n) = 1 - \tfrac{3h}{2} + \tfrac{h^2}{2} be the single-wrap normal-form net coefficients of the proton [u,u,d] and neutron [u,d,d] in H_3(q) (from Quarks as Borromean-linked unknots in the exceptional divisor). For any trace difference \Delta\mathrm{tr},

\mathfrak{E}_0 \cdot \mathrm{net}(p) \cdot \Delta\mathrm{tr} \;=\; \mathfrak{Q}_\beta \cdot \frac{\Delta\mathrm{tr}}{h}.

The deuteron binding functional \mathfrak{E}_0\,(1-\tfrac{h}{2})\,\Delta\mathrm{tr} dresses the energy scale \mathfrak{E}_0 by the proton net coefficient \mathrm{net}(p). It is related to the \beta-decay Q-value \mathfrak{Q}_\beta by the single Hecke factor h.

Context. The trace-canonical deuteron binding on the \mathfrak{E}_0 route over-binds by +11.99\%. Dressing it by (1-\tfrac{h}{2}) corrects it to +0.12\% of AME2020 without fitted constants. The term (1-\tfrac{h}{2}) is exactly \mathrm{net}(p).

The derivation is exact in the field. The key identity is division-free:

\Delta(\mathrm{net}) \;=\; \mathrm{net}(n) - \mathrm{net}(p) \;=\; -\,h \cdot \mathrm{net}(p),

which holds since (1 - \tfrac{3h}{2} + \tfrac{h^2}{2}) - (1 - \tfrac{h}{2}) = -h + \tfrac{h^2}{2} = -h(1-\tfrac{h}{2}). In the substrate regime 0 < h < 2, the proton coefficient \mathrm{net}(p) > 0. Then |\Delta(\mathrm{net})| = h\,\mathrm{net}(p). The Q-value ansatz \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = |\Delta(\mathrm{net})|\,\mathfrak{E}_0 from Symbolic Q-value of free neutron decay yields:

\mathfrak{Q}_\beta \;=\; \mathfrak{E}_0 \, h \, \mathrm{net}(p).

Dividing by h \neq 0 and multiplying by \Delta\mathrm{tr} yields the proposition. The binding dressing \mathrm{net}(p) and the Q-value differ by the factor h = q - q^{-1}, which is bar-odd. Neither side has a definite bar parity: the bar-involution sends h to -h, hence \mathrm{net}(p) = 1 - \tfrac{h}{2} to 1 + \tfrac{h}{2}. The relation is therefore a factor of h, not an instance of the even/odd split conjectured in The binding trace and the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta residue are the bar-even and bar-odd parts of one fibre element.

Scope. The identities are exact. The magnitude claim B_D \approx \mathfrak{E}_0\,\mathrm{net}(p)\,\Delta\mathrm{tr} remains an observation. It accurately models the deuteron (+0.12\%), but does not extend to A \geq 3 because the extensive deficit acts as a separate mechanism. This isolates the origin of (1-\tfrac{h}{2}) to the proton normal-form net coefficient, linking it to the \beta-decay sector. The \Delta_\lambda gate remains the general binding law.
